newsitem.title: USA: Camden, N.J., schools see no state takeover - paper.
newsitem.headline: Camden, N.J., schools see no state takeover - paper.

text.p: Camden County, N.J., schools superintendent Win Tillery said he does not expect the state to take over the problem-plagued Camden School District, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Tuesday.
Tillery said the district can avoid takeover by implementing the recommendations of a report set for release Wednesday.

The report follows a similar analysis last month by the state, which identified about $32 million in possible savings for the district's $200 million budget. That report included a scathing criticism of district operations and budget practices.
The new report was commissioned after the district failed to win certification from the state's Department of Education. The absence of certification can lead to a state takeover.
